keyword: what happens if i miss the tax deadline

verifications.claim: The Failure to File penalty is 5% of unpaid taxes per month, up to 25%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The penalty for failing to file a tax return is 5% of the unpaid tax per month... maximum penalty of 25%" (R1); "5% of the unpaid taxes for each month... maximum penalty of 25%" (R2); "late filing penalty is 5%... maximum penalty is 25%" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the failure-to-file (late filing) penalty as 5% per month or part of month, capped at 25%.

verifications.claim: The Failure to Pay penalty is 0.5% of unpaid taxes per month.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "penalty for filing taxes late is generally 0.5% per month... unpaid tax" (R1); "late-payment penalty is 0.5% of the unpaid balance for each month" (R3); "failure-to-pay penalty... 0.5% of any taxes owed" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the failure-to-pay penalty as 0.5% per month on unpaid taxes.

verifications.claim: The Late Filing Penalty amounts to 5% of the unpaid tax balance for each month or partial month the return is late, capped at 25%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "5% of the unpaid tax per month or part of a month" (R1); "5%... for each month or part of the month... maximum of 25%" (R2); "5%... each month (or part of a month)" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources use 'late filing' interchangeably with 'failure to file' and directly match 5% per month/partial month, capped at 25%.

verifications.claim: The Late Payment Penalty is 0.5% of the unpaid taxes for each month, capped at 25%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "0.5% per month... maximum penalty of 25%" (R1); "0.5%... for each month... as high as 25%" (R3); "0.5%... maximum 25% penalty total" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state late payment (failure to pay) penalty as 0.5% per month, capped at 25%.

verifications.claim: The IRS charges interest around 7% on unpaid taxes.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "interest rate... It's 6% for the quarter beginning April 1, 2026" (R3); "the IRS interest rate is currently 7%" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources provide conflicting rates: 6% in R3 and 7% in R4 for underpayment interest.

verifications.claim: Interest on unpaid taxes is compounded daily from the deadline.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "interest accrues... and compounds daily from April 15" (R3); "interest is compounded daily" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm daily compounding of interest starting from the deadline.

verifications.claim: If a tax return is over 60 days late, the minimum penalty is $525 or 100% of the unpaid tax, whichever is less.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "minimum penalty is $525 or the balance of your taxes due, if less" (R4); "minimum penalty is 100% of the underpayment... more than $500" (R5); "$525 or 100% of the tax owed, whichever is less" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the minimum penalty for returns over 60 days late as $525 or 100% of unpaid tax (whichever less).

verifications.claim: If the IRS owes you money, there is no penalty for filing late.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "due a tax refund... no penalty associated with filing late" (R1); "due a tax refund... IRS doesn't penalize" (R3); "expecting money back... no penalties for filing late" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources consistently state no late-filing penalty if owed a refund.

verifications.claim: Taxpayers have only three years to claim a refund.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "up to three years from the tax-filing deadline to... receive your refund" (R1); "three-year window following the original filing deadline" (R2); "three years to file... before the IRS turns your tax refund over" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm the three-year limit to claim a refund.
